passages.text: And in prayers one must also confess that one has taken refuge in God and solemnly affirm that, on the demon’s part, it is not disobedience but delay. For everything comes to pass for the one who believes, but nothing for the one who does not believe. Hence the demons themselves, knowing the quantity of faith possessed by those whom they overpower, allot a proportionate measure of their own persistence. For this reason they persist with those who do not believe, linger with those who have difficulty believing, but cannot remain even for an instant with those who have believed completely and act well. For the soul, having been turned by faith toward God as though into the nature of water, extinguishes the demon like a spark of fire. It is therefore difficult for each person to recognize the flight of the demon within them. For by blending themselves with souls, the demons suggest to each person’s mind thoughts directed toward whatever they wish, so that the person neglects their own salvation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: that one has taken refuge in God
lexical_decisions.rationale: The perfect infinitive presents recourse to God as an accomplished act with a continuing state.

lexical_decisions.chosen: not disobedience but delay
lexical_decisions.rationale: The contrast concerns the demon’s delayed departure rather than outright refusal.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the quantity of faith
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording explicitly presents faith as possessing a measurable degree or amount.

lexical_decisions.chosen: linger with those who have difficulty believing
lexical_decisions.rationale: δύσπιστος denotes difficulty or reluctance in believing, distinguished here from outright unbelief.

lexical_decisions.chosen: It is therefore difficult
lexical_decisions.rationale: κάματος literally denotes labor or weariness and here characterizes recognition as laborious or difficult.

passages.text: Hence many, not knowing the source by which they are being acted upon, assent to the evil notions suggested by demons as though these were the reasoning of their own soul. Therefore they become more reluctant to go to those capable of saving them, and, while being consumed by the very demons lying in wait for them, they remain unaware. The demons lurking in the innermost recesses of their souls prompt them to suppose that it is not a demon troubling them but a bodily disease—such as acrid matter, bile, phlegm, an imbalance of blood, inflammation of the meninges, or something else—. . . . But even if this were so, not even that is exempt from being a form of demon. For the universal and earthy soul, which passes through all foods as their cause, when taken in to a greater extent through more abundant food, itself unites with the spirit as something kindred to it—the spirit being the soul of a human being—while the material portion of the food, once united with the body, is smeared upon it like a terrible poison. Therefore self-sufficiency is good in everything.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the source by which they are being acted upon
lexical_decisions.rationale: The passive verb describes an agency operating upon them, while πόθεν asks its source.

lexical_decisions.chosen: demons lurking in the innermost recesses
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνδομυχέω depicts dwelling or hiding deep within an interior recess.

lexical_decisions.chosen: acrid matter
lexical_decisions.rationale: In the medical list ὕλη denotes bodily matter or material; “acrid humor” is possible but would impose a more specific technical sense.

lexical_decisions.chosen: being a form of demon
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase categorizes the proposed bodily condition as a manifestation or kind of demon within the author’s framework.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ γὰρ καθόλου καὶ γεώδης ψυχή
lexical_decisions.chosen: For the universal and earthy soul
lexical_decisions.rationale: καθόλου and γεώδης characterize this soul as universal and earth-associated; “general terrestrial soul” is a viable alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: self-sufficiency
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this dietary context αὐτάρκεια may imply contentment or moderation, but its broader sense is sufficiency or self-sufficiency.

source_issues.source_quote: καὶ τοὺς ὑπ’ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐνεδρευόντων δαιμόνων ἀναλισκόμενοι ἀγνοοῦσιν
source_issues.issue: The accusative article τοὺς does not agree with the nominative participle ἀναλισκόμενοι or straightforwardly fit the clause. The translation understands the same people as being consumed while remaining unaware. Deleting τοὺς is a plausible localized conjecture, but the supplied reading is retained and disclosed as grammatically irregular.
source_issues.proposed_reading: καὶ ὑπ’ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐνεδρευόντων δαιμόνων ἀναλισκόμενοι ἀγνοοῦσιν

source_issues.source_quote: ἢ ἄλλου τινός) . . . . εἰ δὲ καὶ τοῦτο ἦν
source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints a lacuna marked by exactly four dots. Its content is unavailable, and no restoration has been supplied; the same four-dot gap remains explicit in the translation.

passages.text: Some of the wicked demons lie in wait in another way. At first they do not even reveal that they exist, so that no effort against them may arise; but when an opportunity comes, under the pretext of anger, erotic passion, or something else, they suddenly assault the body by a sword, a noose, a precipice, or some other means. And, after entering the purifying fire, as we said, they put the deceived souls of those who have been mingled with them in a state of being punished to the end. Others, being ambushed in another way, do not approach us, because they are deceived by the thoughts of the wicked demons into supposing that they suffer these things from their own gods because of their neglect toward them, that they can reconcile those gods through sacrifices, and that they must not approach us but, on the contrary, must flee and hate us. And all the same, they hate and flee those who have greater compassion for them and pursue them in order to benefit them.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν ἀρχὴν οὐδὲ ὅτι εἰσὶν ἐνφαίνοντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: At first they do not even reveal that they exist
lexical_decisions.rationale: τὴν ἀρχήν can mean “at the beginning” or idiomatically “at all”; the subsequent reference to an opportune occasion favors a temporal contrast.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὀργῆς προφάσει, ἔρωτος ἢ ἄλλου τινὸς
lexical_decisions.chosen: under the pretext of anger, erotic passion, or something else
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἔρως here denotes passionate or erotic desire, while πρόφασις presents these emotions as pretexts or occasions.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they suddenly assault the body
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνυβρίζω conveys violent mistreatment or outrage against the body.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in a state of being punished to the end
lexical_decisions.rationale: εἰς τέλος may mean “to the end,” “completely,” or, in some contexts, “forever”; the source-transparent wording leaves its extent unresolved.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after entering the purifying fire
lexical_decisions.rationale: χωρήσαντες is nominative masculine plural and most directly resumes the demons as grammatical subject. A contextual attachment to the people mingled with them is possible despite the case shift.

lexical_decisions.chosen: And all the same
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὁμῶς can mean “alike” or “all the same”; the latter preserves the ironic contrast with the compassion shown to them.

passages.text: Thus, by hating and fleeing us, they are ensnared, not knowing from what source it comes about that they think things contrary to their own salvation. For neither can we compel them, when they are unwilling, to incline toward salvation—since we do not now have such authority over them—nor can they by themselves recognize the demon’s evil thought, for they do not know from where the thoughts of evil are suggested to them. These are the people whom the demons terrify by appearing in whatever forms they wish. Sometimes they also prescribe treatments for the sick, and in this way they gain among those already deceived a reputation as gods and conceal from most people that they are demons—but not from us, who know their secret, the reason why they do such things, transforming themselves in dreams against those over whom they have authority. Some they terrify; to others they issue oracles, demand sacrifices, and command them to share a feast, so that they may drink down their souls along with them.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to incline toward salvation
lexical_decisions.rationale: νεύω depicts leaning, inclining, or signaling assent rather than merely moving physically.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the demon’s evil thought
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐνθύμησις can denote a thought, consideration, or inward suggestion; the genitive identifies the demon as its source.

lexical_decisions.chosen: prescribe treatments
lexical_decisions.rationale: συντάσσω can mean arrange or prescribe, and θεραπεία here refers to treatment or care for the sick.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they gain ... a reputation as gods
lexical_decisions.rationale: δόξα here is reputation or estimation, while θεῶν expresses the status attributed to them.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἑαυτοὺς κατ’ ὄναρ καθ’ ὧν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ἔχουσι μεταμορφοῦντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: transforming themselves in dreams against those over whom they have authority
lexical_decisions.rationale: The first κατά marks the dream setting; the second can bear the adversative sense “against.” It may alternatively refer more generally to those subject to their power.

lexical_decisions.chosen: so that they may drink down their souls along with them
lexical_decisions.rationale: The souls are the accusative object of συνπίνωσιν. The compound evokes drinking together at the feast while portraying the demons as consuming the participants’ souls.

passages.text: For just as formidable snakes draw sparrows toward themselves with their breaths, so these demons also draw those who partake of their table into their own will, having mixed themselves into their minds through the food and drink. They transform themselves in dreams according to the likenesses of the carved images in order to increase the deception. For the carved image is neither a living creature nor does it possess a divine spirit; rather, the demon that was seen made use of its form. To how many other people have they similarly appeared in dreams, yet when those people met one another while awake and compared what they had seen in the dream, they did not agree? Consequently, that which might appear is no longer a dream; rather, it either belongs to a demon or consists of the soul’s products, with the soul giving the forms back to the paria fears and to desire. Or, when struck in its mind by fear, it gives birth to the forms through dreams. But if you think that the carved images, since they are animate, can perform such things, set them on a balance when its beam is level, place the counterweight on the other pan, and call upon them to become either heavier or lighter. If that happens, they are animate; but it does not happen. If, however, it should happen, such a thing is in that way a god. For even this can happen by the finger of a demon. Worms also move, and they are not called gods.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἱ δεινοὶ ὄφεις τοῖς αὐτῶν πνεύμασιν τοὺς στρουθοὺς ἐπισπῶνται
lexical_decisions.chosen: formidable snakes draw sparrows toward themselves with their breaths
lexical_decisions.rationale: πνεύματα here are the snakes’ breaths or exhalations, and στρουθοί most naturally denotes sparrows or small birds.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: διά γε τῶν βρωτῶν καὶ ποτῶν ἀνακραθέντες αὐτῶν τῷ νῷ
lexical_decisions.chosen: having mixed themselves into their minds through the food and drink
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀνακραθέντες portrays the demons as becoming mixed with the participants’ minds by means of what is eaten and drunk.

lexical_decisions.chosen: according to the likenesses of the carved images
lexical_decisions.rationale: ξόανον is a carved cult image, often wooden, while ἰδέαι here are its visible forms or likenesses.

lexical_decisions.chosen: when those people met one another while awake
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὕπαρ contrasts waking experience with what was experienced in a dream.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: Consequently, that which might appear is no longer a dream
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering takes ἐκεῖνο as the subject associated with optative ἐπιφανείη and ὄναρ as the predicate of ἐστιν. The construction is irregular, and other divisions are possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: it gives birth to the forms through dreams
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀποκυΐσκω uses the image of conceiving or giving birth, here applied to the soul’s production of dream forms.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ δὲ ἔσται, οὕτω τὸ τοιοῦτο θεός ἐστιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: If, however, it should happen, such a thing is in that way a god
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected text and punctuation present this as a statement. The surrounding reductio could support hearing it rhetorically, but a question is not imposed on the main text.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by the finger of a demon
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering retains the concrete image of a demon’s finger as the means by which the apparent change could be produced.

source_issues.source_quote: ὥστε οὐκέτι ὄναρ ἐπιφανείη ἐκεῖνό ἐστιν
source_issues.issue: The relation of optative ἐπιφανείη, neuter ἐκεῖνο, and ἐστιν is syntactically irregular and permits more than one division. The main rendering treats ἐκεῖνο as what might appear and ὄναρ as the predicate, while alternatives include understanding the phrase more generally as denying that the appearance is merely a dream apparition.

source_issues.source_quote: τοῖς παρίᾳ φόβοις καὶ ἐπιθυμίᾳ ἀποδιδούσης τὰς ἰδέας
source_issues.issue: The printed παρίᾳ does not yield a defensible construction with the plural article and noun in τοῖς ... φόβοις, nor does it provide a secure lexical meaning in context. The translation transliterates it as “paria” rather than silently omitting or replacing it. Because no defensible English meaning can be established for this surviving printed word, this remains a publication-blocking source problem.

source_issues.source_quote: ἢ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα
source_issues.issue: The printed ἢ can be retained as a disjunctive “or,” as in the main text, but ἡ is also a plausible conjecture because the feminine participle πληγεῖσα naturally refers to the soul: “For the soul, when struck in its mind by fear.” The supplied ἢ has not been silently replaced.
source_issues.proposed_reading: ἡ γὰρ φόβῳ τὸν νοῦν πληγεῖσα
